obtained.how: open-access PDF from the publisher (Journal of Limnology, PAGEPress)

bibliography.note: J. Limnol. 71(1): 170–179 (2012), doi:10.4081/jlimnol.2012.e18; Crossref's page '18' is the article number. Authors as in the entry.

claims.claim: (a perch lays its clutch as one ribbon, so) a bad site 'may easily result in complete failure'
claims.quote: may easily result in complete failure of reproduction
claims.conditions: a general statement in the introduction: 'A mistake in the selection of an appropriate site, substrate or depth for spawning'

claims.claim: 96 sunken trees took two-thirds of all perch strands
claims.location: p. 172 (PDF p. 3), Methods; p. 174 (PDF p. 5), Results; p. 177 (PDF p. 8), Discussion
claims.quote: two thirds of all the egg strands, which were found during the five weeks
claims.conditions: Eurasian perch, Chabařovice Lake (a flooded opencast mine, Czech Republic), 3 May–3 June 2010; the 96 trees (2-m green and dry Norway spruce and silver birch) were artificial spawning substrate the researchers anchored at 1–15 m on two shores; 80 of 124 strands were on them (50 + 30) and 44 elsewhere; the lake's natural substrates had largely degraded or lay too deep
claims.note: 'Sunken trees' should say they were installed for the study, in a lake short of natural substrate; the authors also conclude that depth and site choice 'are not dependent on the presence of suitable spawning substrates' (p. 177).

claims.claim: live soft plants are used only when rigid dead substrate is scarce (Čech 2012: 6–29 % of strands while dead reed beds stood, 77 % once they were gone)
claims.quote: only 6.0-28.9% of egg strands were found to be deposited on live submerged vegetation
claims.conditions: 77.3 % = share of the 44 strands found OUTSIDE the artificial trees in 2010 that lay on live Eurasian water milfoil and stonewort; 6.0–28.9 % = 2007–2009, as reported in Čech et al. 2009–2011; the dead common reed and worm weed (Artemisia) beds had 'gradually disappeared' or lay too deep
claims.note: The 2007–2009 range is Čech 2012 quoting its own earlier papers.

notes: Other values: egg-strand depth rose from 4.9 m to 12.3 m over the season, tracking the 10–12 °C layer and then day length; 92.5–95.5 % of strands deeper than 3 m and none shallower than 1 m (wind and waves); perch preferred the calm shore 50:30 and 34:10; 84 % of strands came from females ≥ 200 mm SL; strands fell from 896 (2007) to 124 (2010) as large females declined under stocked pike and wels predation. This is a deep (≥ 15 m), wind-exposed mine lake, so its depths do not transfer to Hot Brook. For §3.6.1's 'laid mainly on dead pondweed and reed': Čech 2012 names beds of dead common reed and worm weed as the most important substrate; dead pondweed must come from Čech et al. 2009.
